armorSets.name: Musketeer's Armour
armorSets.purpose: The Musketeer set has fairly lackluster bonuses and so it's recommended to focus more on obtaining a great Carnifex set.

spells.fillerNotes: Amya's guide has no single fixed CORE list for Musket - it's structured entirely around named build variants, each with its own implied 4-skill loadout (see Builds). The wiki's Skill Selection tip supplies the underlying loadout logic instead: Blackpowder Grenade is near-mandatory (almost always the paragon pick); choose exactly one of Skirmisher or Close Combat as the control-removal/escape tool; then branch into either the hero-killing pair (Scatter Shot + Fine Gunpowder) or the support pair (Liquid Fire + Deploy Caltrops) for the remaining slots. - wiki

builds.name: LiquidFire / Scatter Shot
builds.summary: The most fully described build - emerged after Zykalian Militia gained popularity. Position at range/highground, throw Liquid Fire into grouped fragile units. One-shots Zykalian Militia, T3 archers, Rattan Marksmen outright; against Falconetti Gunners/Shenji Grenadiers/Flamers/T4 archers, adapt bomb count to target count.

builds.name: Reload
builds.summary: Commonly used in Deathmatch and tournament formats (1v1, 2v2, 5v5), though it can also be fun in siege battles. Same core kit as the LiquidFire build plus one swap into the reload skill (Fine Gunpowder) to extend the hero-kill combo chain.

builds.name: Blue Tier-lock
builds.summary: Posted 2025-09-19. Leverages the fact that during blue tier lock, all units are flammable, all units have low HP pools, and range is spammed heavily - heroes are very low impact, so musket having insane impact on units while being safe as a range + medium is what makes it so good.

builds.name: Full HP (Bomb Build)
builds.summary: Not a separate skill loadout - Amya's freshest-dated post (2026-04-06) argues HP over Agility/Strength for the bomb build in the current low-skirmish meta: more room for risky dives, less chance of a random one-shot, and it costs nothing since your job is Liquid Fire on units, not dueling heroes. "Agi/str doing any difference is kinda copium for 95% of cases."

matchups.why: heavy, low-mobility weapon classes are at a disadvantage dueling a Musket. (wiki)

matchups.vs: Zykalian Militia, T3 archers, Rattan Marksmen
matchups.why: one-shot via Liquid Fire - fragile, low-HP, burn-vulnerable, and they explode on a burn death for bonus AoE. Corroborated from the target's side: Zykalian Militia's own unit guide warns players to "be careful about musket liquid fire, divers, and fire rune interactions."
Blackpowder Grenade and Liquid Fire are themselves ranged skills, so a Musket user can punish large stacks of lightly armoured ranged troops at low personal risk.

an independent Spear Sergeant unit guide names "musket bomb" alongside trebuchet and scorpion fire as one of the siege-AoE templates that punishes a unit sitting in Sheltron (circle) formation. [unverified - doesn't distinguish Blackpowder Grenade from Liquid Fire]

matchups.vs: Chain Dart & Scimitar, Pike, Dual Blades
matchups.why: sprinting and rolling both interrupt an in-progress musket reload, so these high-mobility dueling classes give Musket the most trouble in a duel.

matchups.vs: Falconetti Gunners, Shenji Grenadiers, Flamers, T4 archers
matchups.why: don't one-shot via Liquid Fire - requires matching bomb count to target count to avoid over-spreading the damage.

Musket can't put out consistent unit damage/control compared to other melee classes (Nodachi, Poleaxe), so tanky infantry is hard to deal with. (wiki) [unverified beyond the wiki - Men-at-Arms's own Counters section doesn't itself name Musket or ranged classes]

"musket units" are named among the high-value backline targets worth a surprise flanking charge once caught out of position. (independent Condottieri Guards unit guide) [unverified - not distinguished from other ranged hero classes]

Men-at-Arms's own Veterancy field names Musket directly: "If you can't help your unit (light armor, or medium such as musket): Bot Line..." - a Men-at-Arms unit escorted by a Musket player should run Bot Line veterancy.

Javelin Sergeants' own unit guide documents siege gameplay combining javelin throws with hero weapon skills (spear ultimate, musket shot) for kill confirms. [unverified - exact Musket ability not named beyond "musket shot"]

the house's Civil War custom training-event ruleset (grey armour, grey Musket only, auto-attacks only, no abilities, no horses, no healing, no HUD) pairs Musket with exactly these three units as its designated skill-building drill loadout. - house playbook
no dedicated house or Amya list of units that pair with a Musket player's own warband was found. [GAP: explicit own-warband unit pairings for Musket players - vets/house question]

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk.

techniques.name: Insane Combo (bomb-CC lockdown)
steps: Land an auto-attack in the brief window right before a bomb-CC'd target would naturally rise
staggering resets their get-up timer to instant
techniques.rhythm: keeps a bomb-CC'd target locked instead of giving them a recovery window - The trick is to land an AA during the small frame before they get up, allowing you to hit them quickly without giving them time to recover. This timing is crucial to maximize damage output while keeping the target locked in the combo.

gameplay.text: Inflicts extremely high damage at mid-range, but some attacks have a long reload. Carries several throwing weapons to disrupt the enemy.

The Musket is an early modern firearm which itself boasts high piercing damage and piercing penetration. Musket skills are versatile and can either be selected for a duelling focus, or more commonly, selected for the usage of strong area of effect damage skills with bombs.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.text: If you're in position to hit an enemy hero at all (meaning you are in main push for some reason) you are doing something wrong anyway as you should be flanking / highground if possible to apply pressure for enemy exo/range and buy space for your team.
all units are flammable and low-HP and heroes are comparatively low-impact in that bracket - musket having insane impact on units while being safe as a range + medium is what makes it so good there.

HP give a bit more space to risky move such as deeper dive-in, running near blob to try and throw it into zykalian for example, also make it less likely of being randomly one shot by cav/stalwart, allow you to jump out of wall without dying and make it so enemy DB/CD can't kill u in 1 combo anymore.
Blackpowder Grenade is near-mandatory; Five Rounds Rapid (the other paragon option) has little use against units, a noticeable windup, and is easy to interrupt.

bullets.lead: Pick exactly one of Skirmisher or Close Combat -
bullets.text: for control-effect removal - Skirmisher usually wins out for the escape against high-mobility duelists (Chain Dart & Scimitar, Pike, Spear, Dual Blades); Close Combat trades that escape for a lower cooldown and a melee-range retaliation knockdown.
Despite being a ranged weapon, damage falls off sharply with range - close the distance for good damage rather than kiting at max range.
Headshots increase damage; aim for them wherever possible.
Deploy Caltrops, Blackpowder Grenade, and Liquid Fire can all blunt a cavalry charge.

Blackpowder Grenade and Liquid Fire hit especially hard against ranged infantry specifically because they're themselves ranged skills - punish large stacks of lightly armoured ranged troops at low personal risk.
Liquid Fire is especially strong against low-tier units with weak fire resistance, which matters most in the early seasonal phases when only silver-era-and-below units are available.

bullets.lead: Blackpowder Grenade's "thrown" status can't be removed by hero skills -
bullets.text: a reliable duel opener: throw it, then safely close in and finish with Scatter Shot + Fine Gunpowder.
aim the follow-up at the body, not the head, after an initial headshot auto-attack - the shot spread can whiff a head-aimed Scatter Shot.
Agility is favored over Blunt Damage on the LiquidFire/Scatter Shot build specifically for follow-up speed, despite Blunt's higher raw kill potential on weak units.
Agi/str doing any difference is kinda copium for 95% of cases - we are on a meta with nearly 0 dm, no or near 0 skirmish, so the Str/Agi debate barely matters for the bomb build.
main job is Liquid fire on zykalian, and double bomb viper if you can - "+30-50% survability is a better value than killing +1 flame/shenji on bomb every 1 out 10 games."
Musket only requires Medium armour, but the wiki recommends wearing the heaviest armour a build can afford for the extra defenses.

statSpreads.note: Favored over Blunt Damage specifically for auto-attack/Scatter Shot follow-up speed, despite Blunt's higher raw kill potential on weak units.

combos.name: Headshot-into-Scatter
steps: aim from above their head, lowering slowly until aim-assist shows the red headshot circle
Scatter Shot aimed at the body, not the head
combos.note: The standard hero-killing combo. Aiming the scatter shot at the head can result in a miss due to its spread, so it's safer to target the body.

combos.name: Dive-and-burn
steps: position on high ground or a flank at range
throw Liquid Fire onto grouped fragile targets
combos.note: The blast plus fire DoT can outright delete Zykalian Militia, T3 archers, and Rattan Marksmen regardless of stack size; against tougher stacks (Falconetti Gunners, Shenji Grenadiers, Flamers, T4 archers) the bomb count has to be matched to target count or the damage spreads too thin to kill.
